title: San Francisco Symphony identity
creator: COLLINS
description: Traditional letterforms become a responsive identity through variable font technology that reacts to sound. Black and white retain the orchestra’s heritage, while a broader palette draws from the Bay Area. The system uses changing typography to express musical energy across communications.
real_world_evidence: The Symphony invited COLLINS to define and express its new vision, and the studio describes collaboration with musicians, staff, audiences and leadership.
glyphkiln_test: Test deterministic variable-font axes, large display type and a coherent family of static compositions.

title: Spotify visual identity
creator: COLLINS
description: The identity treats third-party artist photographs with duotone color, borrowing from music’s screen-printing history. Bold color pairs create tension and energy while the image treatment holds different performers together. It offers a useful reference for unifying varied photographic content without using identical layouts.
real_world_evidence: Spotify invited COLLINS to strengthen its brand against competing music services; the case study describes the resulting identity system.
glyphkiln_test: Test consistent duotone treatment across differently lit photographs and multiple aspect ratios.

title: Mailchimp brand system
creator: COLLINS with Mailchimp Brand Team
description: A yellow-heavy palette, revised monkey mark and logotype sit beside hand-drawn illustrations and unusual photography. The system intentionally balances sophistication with absurdity, using imperfect expressive drawing to preserve the company’s personality while making a broad product portfolio easier to understand.
real_world_evidence: Mailchimp invited COLLINS to clarify its growing offerings; the studio credits the in-house Brand Team as a partner in the new identity.
glyphkiln_test: Test integration of hand-drawn assets, irregular imagery and disciplined type hierarchy.

title: Dropbox brand evolution
creator: COLLINS with Dropbox Brand Studio and partners
description: The identity pairs a geometric diamond-built mark with deliberately unexpected combinations of typography, photography, illustration and color. These collisions express collaborative creativity. Its interest comes from different visual ingredients interacting inside one system, rather than from a single decorative background repeated everywhere.
real_world_evidence: Dropbox leadership invited COLLINS to help position the business for expansion, and the case study credits Dropbox Brand Studio and implementation partners.
glyphkiln_test: Test layered compositions with dissimilar image assets and contrasting type without losing brand consistency.

title: Ogilvy identity
creator: COLLINS
description: The new identity moves from a founder’s signature to a redrawn Baskerville-based wordmark. A ligature-rich typographic language suggests connections between people and ideas. The result offers a restrained heritage reference where small letterform decisions carry much of the brand’s character.
real_world_evidence: Ogilvy invited COLLINS to build a future-facing version of its brand while the organization consolidated its divisions.
glyphkiln_test: Test precise serif metrics, ligatures and small-scale wordmark fidelity.

title: Rakbank identity
creator: Koto
description: A refined sail-inspired mark sits alongside a brighter red palette. Handwritten and digital typography express the combination of personal service and digital banking; the script includes Latin and Arabic forms. The identity extends into a launch campaign and physical and digital banking applications.
real_world_evidence: Koto states Rakbank commissioned strategy, architecture, visual and verbal identity, a TV commercial and launch campaign.
glyphkiln_test: Test Arabic shaping, right-to-left layout, bilingual lockups and script ligatures.

title: Norton Museum of Art identity
creator: Koto
description: An archival wordmark supplies a forty-degree angle that becomes a graphic slash throughout the system. A revived Diana seal adds institutional history. Artwork and bright Florida-inspired color interact with typography across banners, stationery and a website whose palette responds to featured collections.
real_world_evidence: Koto describes working with museum staff and leadership on an identity applied to exhibition communications, the museum environment and its website.
source_title: The Norton Museum of Art | Koto
glyphkiln_test: Test image-derived palettes and a repeatable diagonal layout across posters, cards and digital headers.

title: Yazio identity
creator: Koto
description: Yettie, a friendly horned and clawed character, turns healthy habit messaging into an approachable visual world. Bold typography, bright color and playful movement support the mascot. The character appears across the product, campaigns and merchandise rather than remaining an isolated logo illustration.
real_world_evidence: Yazio’s team approached Koto for a refreshed brand; Koto says it worked with the product team to bring the identity into the app.
glyphkiln_test: Test consistent mascot placement and expression variants across promotional and instructional graphics.

title: Deezer identity
creator: Koto
description: A beating-heart symbol anchors a system of adaptable graphic beats. Those beats become patterns, textures and framing elements rather than one fixed background. The identity extends from digital products and playlist artwork to social channels, partnerships and live music events.
real_world_evidence: Koto reports that the refreshed identity launched with Deezer’s enhanced app and web experience and extended across its wider ecosystem.
glyphkiln_test: Test repeatable pattern grammar that varies density and scale across a campaign sequence.

title: Uniqode identity
creator: Koto
description: A custom typeface joins points into a connected visual canvas. Thread-like patterns, square motifs and iconography repeat that construction metaphor across dashboards, campaigns and sales presentations. Blue, purple and pixel-like forms appear in the source’s image descriptions, supporting a crafted digital identity.
real_world_evidence: Koto describes creating the strategy and identity for Uniqode, formerly Beaconstac, and applying it to its product and sales communications.
glyphkiln_test: Test pixel-aligned motifs, custom fonts and a shared visual system for charts and presentation slides.

title: Eko Health identity
creator: Mucho
description: A pulsing lower-case e makes a living, breathing metaphor for the cardiac technology brand. Messaging, product and lifestyle photography, icons and campaign graphics connect medical expertise with accessible technology. The case study shows the system applied to business cards, boxes, the website and a launch poster.
real_world_evidence: Mucho states it collaborated with Eko’s in-house team; Eko’s creative director credits the identity and CORE 500 launch campaign.
glyphkiln_test: Test one line-based motif across packaging, icons and a product launch poster.

title: Visa identity system
creator: Mucho with Commercial Type
description: A flexible grid based on thirds extends the familiar blue, white and yellow identity across differently shaped surfaces. A custom humanist typeface supports small-size reading and multiple languages. Icons grow into illustrations, while cutout and editorial photographs provide different levels of storytelling.
real_world_evidence: Mucho says Visa commissioned a new identity system and includes a testimonial from Visa’s chief brand executive.
source_title: Visa: A symbol of change | Mucho
glyphkiln_test: Test reusable ratio-based layouts and legible multilingual text from payment cards to billboards.

title: Gobi Cashmere identity
creator: Mucho
description: Four interlocking heart forms represent the brand’s goats, herders, employees and customers. A bespoke wordmark and geometric typography accompany symbols inspired by historical Mongolian livestock marks. The system connects labels, tissue, shopping bags and seasonal lookbooks with the brand’s local production story.
real_world_evidence: Gobi approached Mucho for a global repositioning; the case study records workshops in Mongolia and a testimonial from Gobi’s chief executive.
glyphkiln_test: Test culturally specific vector symbols across small tags, repeating tissue patterns and editorial pages.

title: Aeroméxico visual language
creator: Mucho
description: Horizontal repetition grows from the stripes in the airline’s existing logotype. This graphic rhythm connects posters, illustration, digital interfaces and travel communications. The source emphasizes warmth and clarity across the customer journey, with guidelines intended to make a large organization’s applications coherent.
real_world_evidence: Mucho describes designing the visual identity assets and guidelines and conducting adoption sessions with Aeroméxico departments.
glyphkiln_test: Test stripe-based compositions with Spanish copy and consistent hierarchy across wide and portrait layouts.

title: Qynda identity
creator: Mucho
description: A heartbeat-inspired symbol and desert-wind references express motion and resilience for modest sportswear. Red, maroon and pink serve fashion communications, while black and white support sportswear. Focused typography and a planned social content system combine garment information with community and lifestyle subjects.
real_world_evidence: Mucho states it helped establish the Kuwaiti women’s sports brand through strategy, naming and identity, including a system for its social media manager.
glyphkiln_test: Test a coordinated feed mixing product posts, informational posts and photography with a fluid brand motif.

title: Target up&up packaging system
creator: COLLINS with Target Creative Team
description: A unified logotype links a broad private-label range, while category-specific palettes and quality cues distinguish beauty, household and other products. Strong color blocks improve shelf recognition. The system is a useful reference for maintaining one brand across many product shapes and information requirements.
real_world_evidence: COLLINS states it worked with Target on the up&up redesign as Target reformulated products and expanded the range.
glyphkiln_test: Test batch generation of many SKUs with category tokens, variable copy and preserved information hierarchy.

title: Vitaminwater identity and labels
creator: COLLINS
description: The identity builds from the brand’s familiar pharmaceutical-inspired label and irreverent voice. It emphasizes flavor variety as a organizing idea for a broad product range. The reference is especially useful for comparing how stable label architecture can accommodate changing names, flavor descriptions and variants.
real_world_evidence: Vitaminwater’s leadership asked COLLINS to revitalize its positioning and identity; the case study connects the work to subsequent flavor launches.
glyphkiln_test: Test label families with fixed typography hierarchy and unusually long flavor names.

title: Babyganics packaging identity
creator: COLLINS
description: Elemental illustrations draw from Mary Blair’s approach to childhood imagery. They bring gentle scenes to care products while a navigation system uses color, icons and hierarchy to distinguish the range. The design balances emotional friendliness with the practical need to identify a product quickly.
real_world_evidence: COLLINS describes the Babyganics relaunch, expanded retail presence and its own illustration and navigation system for the brand.
glyphkiln_test: Test consistent illustration style and clear category navigation across bottles and cartons.

title: Archer Farms coffee packaging
creator: COLLINS
description: A consistent grid at the top of each pack separates product name, flavor and origin. Below it, commissioned illustrations communicate the places and conditions where coffee grows. This creates visual variety across a crowded assortment while retaining a dependable location for comparison information.
real_world_evidence: Target partnered with COLLINS to reimagine its Archer Farms coffee offering, which the case study identifies as sold exclusively at Target.
glyphkiln_test: Test a fixed information band combined with varied illustrations across coffee SKUs.

title: Cora packaging system
creator: COLLINS
description: A direct manifesto becomes a recurring element across boxes for a varied care range. Restrained typography and tactile finishing support a premium presentation, while simplified ingredients and clearer navigation help shoppers scan. The packaging turns brand language into a repeatable compositional component.
real_world_evidence: COLLINS describes working with founder Molly Hayward as Cora prepared for distribution through Target, CVS and other mass-market retailers.
glyphkiln_test: Test long manifesto text, small functional details and product navigation within limited carton panels.

title: Kungfu Pu’er Tea packaging
creator: Design Bridge and Partners
description: A simplified swordsman mark translates the Wuxia knight into a contemporary symbol. Packaging and communications reinterpret traditional Chinese watercolor, calligraphy, sculpture, rice paper and seal carving. The reference combines a culturally grounded mark with tactile visual textures for a younger tea audience.
real_world_evidence: The studio identifies Kungfu Pu’er as a Yunnan tea producer and describes its commissioned repositioning, identity and packaging work.
source_title: Kungfu Pu’er Tea | Design Bridge and Partners
glyphkiln_test: Test Chinese typography, textured print surfaces and a consistent hierarchy around a detailed cultural symbol.

title: Pastiglie Leone packaging
creator: Design Bridge and Partners
description: The wordmark borrows from Turin street lettering, while decorative patterns use the shapes of the candies themselves. A gold L seal comes from the family archive. These elements unify a broad confectionery portfolio without erasing its distinctive Italian historical character.
real_world_evidence: Design Bridge and Partners describes creating the brand and packaging for the established Turin confectionery manufacturer.
source_title: Pastiglie Leone | Design Bridge and Partners
glyphkiln_test: Test repeatable pattern generation from product shapes, foil-layer artwork and flavor variants.

title: Marabou packaging and identity
creator: Design Bridge and Partners with INGO Sweden
description: The brand’s M becomes an expressive icon that changes character with different flavors and moods. A strongly yellow visual world ties the portfolio together. This is a reference for giving an established packaged-goods identity greater range through a single recognizable letterform.
real_world_evidence: The studio states it worked with Marabou and INGO Sweden; the page includes a testimonial from Marabou’s senior brand manager.
glyphkiln_test: Test a flexible letterform motif across a family of wrappers without reducing product-name clarity.

title: All Good Scents fragrance packaging
creator: Mucho
description: A perfume-pyramid logo unifies a range with deliberately varied visual treatments. Essentials use blurred pictograms; premium variants introduce eighties-style strokes, tweed with fluorescent color, earthy gradients and white art-deco patterns with gold. One brand accommodates different olfactory personalities through controlled stylistic variation.
real_world_evidence: Mucho describes creating the identity and packaging for All Good Scents, an Indian contemporary perfume house.
glyphkiln_test: Test one packaging architecture across four markedly different pattern, texture and color directions.

title: Julie’s biscuit packaging refresh
creator: Design Bridge and Partners
description: The refreshed girl symbol and an optimistic yellow palette make the brand recognizable at a distance. The viewed application pairs a yellow handled biscuit bag with a blue-and-yellow character poster, combining stacked product photography, flavor naming and a clearly separated master-brand mark.
real_world_evidence: The studio states it worked alongside Julie’s team, and the case study includes a testimonial from company director Tzy Horng Sai.
glyphkiln_test: Test a mascot-led food pack and coordinated poster with distinct product and brand scales.

title: Figlia olive oil packaging
creator: Design Bridge and Partners
description: Three hundred locally handcrafted ceramic bottles suggest feminine forms. Their shapes inspire a visual language of soft, organic illustrations and minimal faces. The physical vessel and printed graphic language tell the same family story, rather than treating packaging as a rectangular label alone.
real_world_evidence: The studio states it created a brand for Agricola Dargenio’s limited-edition olive oil and worked with a ceramic artist to produce 300 bottles.
glyphkiln_test: Test abstract vector portraits, sparse label composition and graphics presented on irregular product forms.

title: Callaly packaging and identity
creator: Design Bridge and Partners
description: Soft edges and smooth lines echo the body, while the packaging opening mirrors the product experience through a tear strip. Darker and lighter product colors distinguish flow needs. The reference connects graphic navigation, structural packaging and an intentionally visible, confident brand presence.
real_world_evidence: The studio describes designing Callaly’s identity and smart packaging and reports the brand’s move from direct sales into physical stores.
glyphkiln_test: Test tonal variant coding, opening-panel sequencing and clear functional labels on a folded package.

title: Burger King rebrand packaging
creator: Jones Knowles Ritchie
description: The rebrand reconnects the restaurant with its food through a heritage-inspired identity, custom Flame type and a warmer palette. Packaging participates in the same visual system as uniforms and signs. It demonstrates how everyday disposable surfaces can carry a strong typographic personality.
real_world_evidence: JKR identifies the project as Burger King’s rebrand; its official agency record specifies packaging, uniforms and signage as applications.
glyphkiln_test: Test expressive display typography and coherent graphics across wrappers, cups and wide menu surfaces.

title: Manischewitz brand and packaging
creator: Jones Knowles Ritchie
description: Cream and warm orange backgrounds support chunky flared lettering with Hebrew-inspired details. Red line drawings of people and food bring humor to the identity. The reviewed case-study images extend this language onto branded boxes and aprons, supported by richly styled food photography.
real_world_evidence: JKR states Manischewitz asked for help reaching a broader American audience while retaining its Jewish-American heritage and traditions.
glyphkiln_test: Test flared custom lettering, line illustrations and consistent warm color treatment across branded physical goods.

title: Impossible Foods rebrand
creator: Jones Knowles Ritchie
description: Large condensed white lettering and vivid red contrast with deep burgundy. Close-up burgers and meat-style product naming emphasize appetite, while stamped badges and price-poster typography extend the visual world. The inspected graphics use familiar meat-retail cues to reposition plant-based products.
real_world_evidence: JKR presents its identity work for Impossible as a shift intended to appeal to meat eaters, with product graphics shown in the case study.
glyphkiln_test: Test condensed typography, dense price hierarchy, product photography crops and a coordinated SKU family.

title: Citizen
creator: Pentagram — Emily Oberman and Eddie Opara
description: A magazine system documenting Black culture uses a flexible editorial grid, a customized sans-serif masthead, photography, handmade collage and illustration. Its past, present and future sections progressively increase text weight from light to medium to bold, making typography part of the narrative.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram states its teams designed the logo, grid, structure, pacing and complete look of Citizen’s inaugural issue.
glyphkiln_test: Vary typographic weights by section while preserving a coherent multipage grid and image-led pacing.

title: Sight and Sound
creator: Pentagram — Marina Willer
description: The BFI magazine redesign draws on film clapperboards and its own 1970s masthead. Condensed headlines, visible grids, vertical text, circular image crops and section colors create varied pacing, while Big Caslon body copy supports longer reading.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram documents the commissioned redesign and its launch with four covers for the Future of Film issue.
glyphkiln_test: Produce cover variants and editorial spreads with visible grids, rotated headings, image masks and readable long text.

title: Public Speaking
creator: Pentagram — Paula Scher
description: An annual report adopts the scale and character of a souvenir theater program. Performance photographs, Knockout typography and a black, white and red palette organize audience statistics, interviews, patron stories and a timeline tracing the season’s creative collaborations.
real_world_evidence: The Public Theater issued Public Speaking to review its activities during 2013–2014, with editorial design by Pentagram.
glyphkiln_test: Combine narrative spreads, statistics, credits and a dense relationship timeline in one publication.

title: i.Detroit
creator: Studio Sutherl& with Marcus Lyon
description: A research project presents 100 Detroit residents through photographic portraits, ancestral DNA and recorded personal histories. The book connects to an image-activated app, while a seven-inch record extends the project through soundscapes referencing Detroit’s musical history and contemporary streets.
real_world_evidence: Studio Sutherl& documents the three-year collaboration with Marcus Lyon and links to the released app and sound recordings.
glyphkiln_test: Create 100 consistent portrait records with differing personal data and a reliable relationship between print and linked media.

title: Somos Brasil
creator: Studio Sutherl& with Marcus Lyon
description: Portraits and personal histories of more than 100 Brazilians are paired with ancestral DNA data. Graphics derive from separated elements of the Brazilian flag; the book reveals portraits before their associated DNA, and an image-recognition app gives access to each participant’s voice.
real_world_evidence: Studio Sutherl& identifies the produced book, app and exhibition as its collaboration with photographer Marcus Lyon.
glyphkiln_test: Maintain a national geometric vocabulary across portraits, data graphics and sequential reveal spreads.

title: Rijksmuseum in Detail
creator: Irma Boom
description: A museum publication uses fifty foldout sheets to examine collection highlights. Enlarged details and short explanatory text address symbolism, technique, materials, style and historical context, making the physical unfolding of the page part of how readers encounter individual artworks.
real_world_evidence: The Rijksmuseum shop sells the publication and explicitly credits its fifty foldout sheets to Irma Boom.
glyphkiln_test: Design paired overview-and-detail spreads with captions, fold boundaries and consistent print dimensions.

title: The Fendi Set
creator: Graphic Thought Facility
description: A wide photographic book connects Kim Jones’s couture collection with the Bloomsbury group and locations including Charleston, Paris and Rome. Diverse analog images flow with a loose album-like structure, while changes of paper stock emphasize differences in the photographic material.
real_world_evidence: GTF identifies the 2022 publication for Fendi and explains its connection to the Spring/Summer 2021 couture collection.
source_title: Fendi — The Fendi Set — Graphic Thought Facility
glyphkiln_test: Support landscape image sequences with varied image sizes, quiet captions and a flexible rather than uniform grid.

title: Industrial Facility
creator: Graphic Thought Facility
description: The studio monograph turns objects from roughly 200 projects into a connected photographic sequence. Each spread repeats or adds designs from the previous spread, forming a visual chain; seven short interviews and integrated portraits interrupt and enrich the object narrative.
real_world_evidence: GTF lists Phaidon as the publication client and describes designing the first monograph of Industrial Facility’s complete works.
source_title: Phaidon — Industrial Facility — Graphic Thought Facility
glyphkiln_test: Compose a sequence in which recurring objects connect adjacent spreads without forcing identical layouts.

title: Gagosian Quarterly redesign
creator: Graphic Thought Facility
description: A generous magazine format pairs a custom condensed headline face with Berthold Arena for body text. Feature typography can depart from the house style when content requires it. The masthead appears through a die-cut cover aperture whose position responds to each artwork.
real_world_evidence: GTF documents its complete 2016 redesign following a new editorial direction for Gagosian’s established quarterly magazine.
source_title: Gagosian — Gagosian Quarterly — Graphic Thought Facility
glyphkiln_test: Allow publication-level typography with story-specific overrides and artwork-aware cover placement.

title: Creating with Shapes
creator: Graphic Thought Facility
description: Usha Doshi’s fabric experiments are organized into seven chapters based on geometric shapes. Black-and-white photography concentrates attention on form and is supported by instructional drawings. Punched dividers, undyed cloth and a translucent wrapper connect the book’s physical construction to its subject.
real_world_evidence: GTF states that Creating with Shapes was the first book published by COS.
source_title: COS — Creating with Shapes — Graphic Thought Facility
glyphkiln_test: Build instructional sequences combining monochrome photos, technical line illustrations and shape-based chapter navigation.

title: Modern Design Review, issues 1 and 2
creator: Graphic Thought Facility
description: The magazine combines commissioned product photography with flexible templates that allow each feature a separate direction. The first issue’s jacket stages furniture components in flower-arranging foam, connecting its cover concept to an interior story on Ikebana. Custom serif and sans-serif headline faces support its identity.
real_world_evidence: GTF identifies its art direction for the published launch issues and credits editor Laura Houseley and commissioned photographers.
source_title: Modern Design Review — Issues 1 and 2 — Graphic Thought Facility
glyphkiln_test: Test whether a reusable magazine system can accommodate different photographic and typographic directions per article.

title: Interwoven: Kvadrat Textile and Design
creator: Graphic Thought Facility
description: A company history brings together archival material and commissioned photographs of textile mills. Its cover fabric was specially dyed, spun and woven in collaboration with Peter Saville and Wallace Sewell, allowing the company’s core material to become a central part of the publication.
real_world_evidence: GTF identifies the book as a 2014 publication for Kvadrat and details its commissioned photography and specially produced cover cloth.
glyphkiln_test: Combine archival and newly shot imagery while specifying consistent color and typography across cover and interior.

title: The Art of Typewriting
creator: Graphic Thought Facility
description: A publication from the Sackner Archive combines typewriter history, artwork plates and a dense biographical reference section. Each cover pairs two artworks uniquely through a custom algorithm feeding a digital press, making controlled variation an integral part of the production system.
real_world_evidence: GTF lists the 2015 Thames & Hudson publication and explains how its variable covers were produced on an HP Indigo digital press.
source_title: Thames & Hudson — The Art of Typewriting — Graphic Thought Facility
glyphkiln_test: Generate many reproducible cover combinations while preserving credits, title hierarchy and production constraints.

title: The DIOR Sessions
creator: Graphic Thought Facility
description: A collaboration between Kim Jones and Nikolai von Bismarck is presented through portraits photographed on black-and-white film. Torn darkroom test strips become the graphic material for the trade slipcase and special-edition box, representing the collection without selecting a single portrait as its emblem.
real_world_evidence: GTF documents the 2019 Dior publication and the trade and special-edition packaging treatments.
source_title: Dior — The DIOR Sessions — Graphic Thought Facility
glyphkiln_test: Use a shared image archive to produce coherent book, slipcase and box compositions with differing aspect ratios.

title: Chatsworth, Arcadia, Now
creator: Graphic Thought Facility
description: Seven historical periods structure a book about Chatsworth. New photography mixes domestic intimacy with architectural grandeur. Kaleidoscopic chapter patterns originate in details of the house, while historically informed headline letters and contemporary illuminated initials connect the editorial design to the collection.
real_world_evidence: GTF lists the 2021 Penguin Books publication and describes commissioning photography over two years of access to Chatsworth.
source_title: Penguin Books — Chatsworth, Arcadia, Now — Graphic Thought Facility
glyphkiln_test: Derive repeatable patterns from source images and combine ornate initials with readable historical essays.

title: Nike Viz System
creator: Datalands
description: A visualization system distinguishes three communication contexts: simple social content, presentations and marketing reports, and more detailed internal communication. Simplified shapes create a recognizable brand vocabulary, with more than thirty iterations per method exploring clarity across differing information densities.
real_world_evidence: Datalands states that Nike commissioned the rethink in 2022 and that the resulting system informed internal tools.
glyphkiln_test: Render the same dataset at three complexity levels while preserving brand identity and quantitative meaning.

title: Artolution impact visualizations
creator: Pentagram — Giorgia Lupi
description: An animated map and winding timeline explain the nonprofit’s program reach over five years. Color, dots and lines encode project characteristics, while brushstroke-inspired blooms identify locations. The visual language links the data to collaborative public art and supports the organization’s fundraising story.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram states the pair of visualizations was created for Artolution’s 2021 annual report.
glyphkiln_test: Map projects with overlapping attributes and pair geographic information with a readable temporal sequence.

title: IBM Data Visualization Guidelines
creator: Giorgia Lupi and Accurat
description: An online visualization vocabulary extends IBM’s design language across charts, maps, diagrams and animation. Research into practical product scenarios shaped rules for composition and density, while references to punch cards, typewriters and early machines connect the system to IBM’s visual history.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram’s case study says IBM commissioned Lupi’s team in 2016 and publicly released the guidelines in early 2017.
glyphkiln_test: Implement brand-specific chart tokens and rules that remain consistent across many data types and densities.

title: RAND Art + Data residency
creator: Pentagram — Giorgia Lupi
description: Three visualizations translate research on mental health, connected bodily devices and income inequality. Approaches range from brain-inspired colored waves to animation and a layered paper-disc sculpture, demonstrating how the same research institution can communicate through different graphic metaphors and media.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram documents Lupi’s 2021 appointment to the RAND Art + Data Residency and the three resulting projects.
glyphkiln_test: Express different datasets through distinct visual metaphors while retaining legends, source notes and clear interpretation.

title: Goalkeepers design and data system
creator: Pentagram — Giorgia Lupi and team
description: The system uses a 10.6-degree slant derived from the Sustainable Development Goals wheel across images, information containers and typography. Templates range from formal research reports to expressive social posts, and custom chart styles extend the identity into the initiative’s data-led reporting.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram describes a two-year partnership and the refreshed website and visualizations for the 2022 Goalkeepers Report.
glyphkiln_test: Adapt one angular brand system to charts, research pages and social formats without reducing data legibility.

title: Plastic Air
creator: Pentagram — Giorgia Lupi, with Google Arts & Culture
description: An interactive visualization makes airborne microplastics visible through graphic particles and familiar objects. Users alter location or weather and inspect particles for composition and possible origin. The experience deliberately presents an approximation informed by limited research rather than claiming to measure a viewer’s actual air.
real_world_evidence: The project was developed with Google Arts & Culture and released for Earth Day 2021 in its environmental experiment series.
glyphkiln_test: Test shape-coded particles, layered labels, controlled simulation parameters and explicit uncertainty annotations.

title: Discover Forgiveness
creator: Pentagram — Giorgia Lupi, with Accurat
description: Research papers become patches in a digital quilt: color encodes subject themes and geometric patterns indicate geographic regions. Combined criteria produce combined visual treatments. Filters rearrange the patches, and annotations lead from approachable summaries to the original research publications.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram identifies Templeton World Charity Foundation as client and describes the live research collection and updateable database.
glyphkiln_test: Encode multiple categorical attributes with color and pattern while retaining an understandable legend and filtering.

title: Out of Many, One — immigration infographics
creator: Pentagram — Giorgia Lupi
description: Two infographics supplement a portrait book with historical and procedural context. A brushstroke-like timeline encodes immigrant origins over time, while a yes/no flowchart traces routes to citizenship. Secondary measures and annotations add detail without removing the broader narrative structure.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram states that Crown commissioned the infographics for George W. Bush’s published portrait collection Out of Many, One.
glyphkiln_test: Lay out a dense branching process and multiseries timeline with legends, annotation hierarchy and accurate connectors.

title: La Lettura data visualization series
creator: Giorgia Lupi and Accurat
description: Full-spread visualizations for the newspaper’s cultural supplement explore subjects including migration of talent, art prices and Nobel Prizes. Maps, musical scores and original symbols inform the graphic language, while qualitative context supplements numerical evidence to create detailed visual stories.
real_world_evidence: The first-party case study states that La Lettura’s editor invited Lupi, then at Accurat, to create the series with newsroom staff.
glyphkiln_test: Support custom visual encodings, dense legends and related datasets across a newspaper-sized composition.

title: Science Stack: Tools Within Reach
creator: Pentagram — Giorgia Lupi, with Accurat
description: Scientific tools are organized as a digital stack of cards inspired by library catalogs, punch cards and collectible cards. Color, dots and patterns encode attributes including cost, use and openness, enabling readers to sort a complex research ecosystem into approachable comparisons.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram names the Wilson Center as client and describes collaboratively developing the content and data for the infographic.
source_title: Science Stack: Tools Within Reach — Pentagram
glyphkiln_test: Generate comparable cards from structured records with multiple encodings, consistent density and sortable attributes.

title: Spice Market menus and collateral
creator: Pentagram — Emily Oberman
description: A restaurant identity is applied to everyday printed objects for the Southeast Asian restaurant in New York’s Meatpacking District. The case study explicitly presents menus, takeaway containers and matches, offering a compact example of maintaining a recognizable identity across practical hospitality formats.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram identifies Spice Market as the client and captions the produced menu, container and match applications.
glyphkiln_test: Maintain brand recognition and small-text readability across menus, food containers and very small print surfaces.

title: Sussex menus and printed collateral
creator: Random Order
description: A triangular arrangement based on the Sussex county flag becomes a flexible identity for the restaurant. Monospaced Prestige Elite typography and a restrained menu resembling a clothbound book extend across business cards, coasters and posters, with changing six-part motifs responding to different uses.
real_world_evidence: Random Order states that the system is deployed across menus, signage, business cards and event posters for the Gladwin Brothers’ restaurant.
glyphkiln_test: Adapt one geometric layout rule across menus and cards while allowing different icons and content lengths.

title: Parla menu and collateral
creator: Pentagram — Emily Oberman
description: A neighborhood Italian café uses tightly spaced, leaning lettering and bright colors informed by 1960s and 1970s Italian graphics. Round and square pizza shapes organize a poster that also serves as a menu, while related symbols continue across coasters and color-coded box labels.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram states it developed the identity and all collateral for Corner Table Restaurants’ Parla café in New York.
glyphkiln_test: Create a dual-purpose poster-menu and coordinate geometric symbols across small labels and coasters.

title: Agatha Christie commemorative stamps
creator: Studio Sutherl& with Neil Webb
description: Six stamps depict scenes and characters from Agatha Christie novels while embedding clues in microtext, ultraviolet ink and thermochromic ink. The miniature format makes scale and hidden information part of the experience, extending the fiction’s detective logic into a functioning postal object.
real_world_evidence: Studio Sutherl& documents the special stamp issue and links to its Royal Mail retail release.
glyphkiln_test: Test extremely small format illustration, microtype, consistent series borders and separately specified specialty-print layers.

title: Kings Place variable identity and business cards
creator: Studio Sutherl&
description: A sound-driven identity turns music and spoken words into distinct static and animated logotypes. The venue’s wave-shaped architecture informs the concept. Staff selected tracks for individualized business cards, while the shared red and pink palette and typography maintain continuity across the program.
real_world_evidence: Studio Sutherl& states the generator is used by both client and designers and that staff-specific business cards were produced.
glyphkiln_test: Produce deterministic identity variants from a controlled input while maintaining legibility and fixed business-card information.

title: Cooper Hewitt Smithsonian Design Museum
creator: Pentagram — Eddie Opara and Michael Gericke
description: Pentagram developed an identity and environmental program for the renovated Carnegie Mansion. Exterior identification, exhibition directories, donor recognition and wayfinding use the custom Cooper Hewitt typeface, with signs integrated into a protected historic building that could not be physically altered.
real_world_evidence: The studio documents graphics made for the museum’s 2014 reopening following its three-year renovation.
glyphkiln_test: Create consistent room directories, directional signs and object labels from one type system.

title: Garden Museum
creator: Pentagram — Jody Hudson-Powell and Luke Powell
description: The museum’s identity uses deliberately imperfect organic shapes informed by gardens and Roberto Burle Marx. Forms combine into illustrations or separate into icons, while characterful typography and a flexible palette support both restrained institutional communication and more expressive events.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram describes the identity, website and signage created for the museum’s May 2017 reopening.
glyphkiln_test: Generate a coherent family of abstract botanical icons, patterns and directional signs.

title: Princeton University Art Museum
creator: 2x4
description: A bespoke typeface rooted in the museum’s history connects its graphic identity and wayfinding. Donor recognition adapts the letterforms to different materials and fabrication techniques, extending the system throughout the new building and responding to its varied architectural textures.
real_world_evidence: 2x4 states that it partnered with the museum on a graphic identity and comprehensive wayfinding for its new home.
glyphkiln_test: Maintain typographic hierarchy across directories, engraved labels and large architectural signs.

title: MIT Museum Exhibitions
creator: Pentagram — Michael Bierut
description: Nine related graphic approaches distinguish the museum’s galleries while retaining coherence with its institutional identity. Typography responds to scientific subject matter, and the program includes hundreds of exhibition titles, panels and object labels together with custom diagrams and infographics.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram documents exhibition graphics for the museum’s October 2022 reopening in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
glyphkiln_test: Produce a large set of content-variable labels and explanatory diagrams without losing gallery hierarchy.

title: Central Park Conservancy
creator: Pentagram — Michael Bierut
description: A rectangular mark echoes Central Park’s proportions, accompanied by Gotham Condensed and emerald greens. Custom leaf icons become a decorative alphabet and patterns. The signage and map program works alongside existing municipal signs, supporting both visitor navigation and recognition of the nonprofit steward.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram reports collaboration with Conservancy leadership and describes banners installed along park paths.
glyphkiln_test: Combine map keys, directional information and decorative type with consistent hierarchy.

title: Folger Shakespeare Library
creator: Pentagram
description: The refreshed identity supports a broader public program across exhibitions, performances, publications and education. Its reference points include historic lettering on the building, while a comprehensive environmental graphics and signage program accompanies expanded public galleries and accessible entrances.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram identifies the identity and signage as part of the Folger’s 2024 renovation and revitalization.
glyphkiln_test: Adapt historic typographic character into readable multi-level institutional signage.

title: Inequalities at Triennale Milano
creator: Pentagram — Giorgia Lupi
description: Gridded patterns translate datasets about inequality into an identity for the 24th International Exhibition. The system accommodates different statistics within a consistent visual language, extending from exhibition graphics and promotional material to the catalogue, with concise legends explaining the data.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram states that the exhibition opened at Triennale Milano on May 13, 2025 and credits collaboration with its in-house team.
glyphkiln_test: Generate patterns from real numeric datasets while preserving legends, scale and accurate encoding.

title: Cartier at the V&A
creator: Pentagram
description: The exhibition’s graphic system draws from Cartier’s archival printed ephemera, pairing an expressive italic with functional grotesk and engraving-like lettering. Narrow columns and controlled tracking create a historic texture, while inset grooves and relief lettering integrate information with immersive exhibition spaces.
real_world_evidence: The case study states that exhibition architect Asif Khan asked Pentagram to create the identity and graphics for the V&A show.
glyphkiln_test: Test refined multi-font text panels with narrow columns, tracking and consistent caption hierarchy.

title: South Korean Road Signage
creator: Studio Dumbar/DEPT
description: The system reduces information overload through clearer layouts, road numbers, arrows and pictograms. Its custom Hangil typeface uses spacing and optical adjustments designed for reading at speed, with Korean and Roman information coordinated across sign sizes and darkened background colors.
real_world_evidence: Studio Dumbar states that the government invited the studio to redesign road signage and that implementation is proceeding nationwide.
source_title: Studio Dumbar — South Korean Road Signage
glyphkiln_test: Render Korean and Latin labels with robust fallback, spacing, directional arrows and distance-readable hierarchy.

title: TNT Green Office Headquarters
creator: Studio Dumbar/DEPT
description: The signage for TNT’s Green Office uses simple color and material choices to guide visitors without dominating the architecture. Transparent interiors and abundant daylight shape the approach, including privacy foils developed to protect workspace privacy while retaining the building’s light-energy performance.
real_world_evidence: Studio Dumbar identifies a commission to design signage for TNT’s Green Office, opened in Hoofddorp in 2009.
glyphkiln_test: Build consistent room signs, icon families and privacy patterns for different spatial applications.

title: Imperial College Circle of Benefactors
creator: Pentagram — Domenic Lippa and Jon Marshall
description: A donor installation uses cells of colored recycled glass within a modular steel structure. The three roundel sizes and six colors create variation, while each cell bears a donor name. Its cellular organization allows the installation to expand as additional benefactors join.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram describes the completed installation in the reception area of Imperial’s Kensington campus.
source_title: Imperial College London, Circle of Benefactors, Donor Installation
glyphkiln_test: Lay out variable-length names within an expanding modular diagram and preserve balanced spacing.

title: Grand Palais Wayfinding
creator: 2x4
description: The signage system joins a common visual language and naming structure with different materials suited to individual spaces. Exterior elements reference verdigris Art Nouveau metalwork, while interior areas use bronze, terracotta and orange accents to connect a historic landmark with its renewed public role.
real_world_evidence: 2x4 describes its collaboration on visitor experience and integrated signage during the Grand Palais renovation.
glyphkiln_test: Apply one directory structure across palettes and material mockups while retaining hierarchy.

title: Ruhrtriennale
creator: Studio Dumbar/DEPT
description: An opening-and-closing R/T logo expresses the festival as a portal to new perspectives. Custom software creates blurred and pixelated imagery combining organic and digital qualities, while varied colors and motion behavior support a broad program across multiple industrial venues.
real_world_evidence: The studio states that Ruhrtriennale appointed it to develop a new identity for the cultural festival.
glyphkiln_test: Test repeatable blurred/pixelated imagery and a logo framing system across event formats.

title: D&AD Festival 2020 — Imagine Everything
creator: Studio Dumbar/DEPT
description: The identity centers on the word imagine and uses variable Marfa typography that stretches and shifts to express creative possibility. Initially prepared for a physical festival, the system was adapted for digital programming, personalized social posts, category landing pages and winner filters.
real_world_evidence: Studio Dumbar documents its invitation to create the 2020 festival identity and the subsequent move to a fully digital event.
glyphkiln_test: Stress-test variable-width headlines and large campaign batches with personalized copy.

title: Public Design Festival 2023
creator: studio fnt
description: Blue arrows and red and yellow circles form a highly visible graphic language for a national public-design festival. The balanced shapes express safety, prosperity and collective participation. Motion versions stack and move the forms, linking the static identity to an animated festival presence.
real_world_evidence: The studio states that its identity was applied to print and digital touchpoints across the country during the September 2023 festival.
glyphkiln_test: Build multilingual event posters from a controlled shape vocabulary and primary-color palette.

title: NN North Sea Jazz Festival
creator: Studio Dumbar/DEPT
description: A motion-originated identity turns live music’s rhythm into animated and static typography. Custom code drives the text behavior, while the festival’s recognizable green swash remains in place alongside brighter accents and stronger contrasts, balancing established recognition with a broader musical program.
real_world_evidence: Studio Dumbar reports that the refreshed identity debuted in the festival’s promotional campaigns.
source_title: Studio Dumbar — NN North Sea Jazz Festival
glyphkiln_test: Produce rhythmically varied typography with deterministic parameters and consistent event metadata.

title: Amsterdam Sinfonietta Poster Series
creator: Studio Dumbar/DEPT
description: The orchestra’s concert posters use a changing visual approach each season, with different designers responding to musical themes. Individual series can differ radically while retaining recognizable continuity, making the long-running commission an example of sustained art direction rather than one repeated composition.
real_world_evidence: Studio Dumbar describes a decade-long client relationship and posters created to advertise the orchestra’s concerts.
glyphkiln_test: Create a coherent poster series with genuinely different compositions tied to content.

title: Studio Theatre
creator: Pentagram — Abbott Miller
description: Heavy typography and a yellow, black and white palette connect the theater to its former factory home. Campaign posters combine strong type with images, while large illuminated letters, archival photo collages and stage-direction murals extend the same visual character into the building.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram documents its identity, environmental graphics and poster campaigns for Studio Theatre in Washington, DC.
glyphkiln_test: Adapt a theatrical campaign across posters, façade-scale type and dense archival collages.

title: 10th Seoul Record Fair
creator: studio fnt
description: The tenth edition uses X as both a Roman numeral and crossing lines that refer to its two venues. Motion expands an existing motif without adding new colors or forms, responding to digital kiosks at the event while retaining the visual identity’s established logic.
real_world_evidence: The case study names the organizing committee as client and dates the commissioned event graphics to January 2022.
glyphkiln_test: Vary one geometric motif across print and digital compositions without adding decorative noise.

title: Jeonju International Film Festival Identity
creator: studio fnt
description: The identity translates the festival’s existing butterfly-wing motif into a flexible graphic system. Wing movement and colors drawn from flowers connect the spring festival to projected light, creating a visual language that can expand and recombine while retaining a recognizable conceptual basis.
real_world_evidence: studio fnt identifies the project as a new festival identity for Jeonju International Film Festival.
glyphkiln_test: Generate a controlled kaleidoscopic family while preserving an identity’s source motif.

title: Record284 — Culture on a Turntable
creator: studio fnt
description: Vinyl records viewed from multiple perspectives become the identity’s central graphic motif. Saturated colors and changing proportions connect posters, banners, leaflets, venue graphics and souvenirs for an exhibition spread between Seoul Station Plaza, partner spaces and an online platform.
real_world_evidence: studio fnt documents designing the exhibition identity and overseeing production of its souvenir goods for Culture Station Seoul 284.
source_title: Record284 — Culture on a Turntable — studio fnt
glyphkiln_test: Translate one object into multiple viewpoints and apply it across a coordinated event kit.

title: Whitney Museum Graphic Identity
creator: Experimental Jetset with Whitney in-house design team
description: The Responsive W is a four-line zigzag that adapts to available space and artwork proportions while keeping the Whitney name in a fixed relationship. Neue Haas Grotesk provides a stable typographic voice, and instructions guide the museum’s designers in making varied applications.
real_world_evidence: Experimental Jetset describes its commissioned collaboration with the Whitney and credits the museum team responsible for applications.
glyphkiln_test: Test an adaptive vector motif that responds to image geometry without obscuring artwork.

title: Spain Guest of Honour — Frankfurt Book Fair 2022
creator: TwoPoints.Net
client: Spanish Ministry of Culture and Sports
description: Three interchangeable visual gestures express the diversity of Spanish literature and regional languages. Handmade painting is combined with digital 3D animation, allowing a shared concept to take different forms while communicating literary creativity across cultural and geographic boundaries.
real_world_evidence: TwoPoints.Net states that it developed the identity and supervised its application from 2021 for Spain’s 2022 Guest of Honour presentation.
glyphkiln_test: Combine authored paint assets with precise typography and consistent multiformat compositions.

title: Sundance Film Festival
creator: PORTO ROCHA with Sundance Institute design team
description: A film-ratio frame works as both logo and device for highlighting scenes, people and emotions in festival imagery. Filmstrip-inspired compositions, Monument Grotesk and a narrator-like brand voice provide an enduring system that can accommodate diverse films and annual programming.
real_world_evidence: The studio’s case study credits the Sundance Institute team and documents the festival’s commissioned evergreen identity.
glyphkiln_test: Build flexible image-led campaign layouts using aspect-ratio frames and changing content density.

title: The Goodtime Hotel
creator: Base Design
description: A restrained logo and custom lowercase typewriter-style face complement the hotel’s theatrical tropical interiors. The mark references a welcoming gesture and is applied sparingly across guest items, including translucent keys, tissue packets and bathrobes, creating continuity without competing with the setting.
real_world_evidence: Base Design describes its branding for Pharrell Williams and Dave Grutman’s operating South Beach hotel.
glyphkiln_test: Maintain recognition on small translucent, fabric and packaging applications using minimal assets.

title: Bottega
creator: Pentagram — Andrea Trabucco-Campos
description: Sunlight entering the café inspires a system of shifting dots, shadows and perspectives. Variable display type pairs with a quieter text face, and matching illustrations extend through menus, bags, tray paper, packaging, signage and digital touchpoints for the neighborhood business.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram documents the identity and environmental graphics for the Crown Heights café and sandwich shop.
glyphkiln_test: Coordinate a variable typographic and illustrative system across menus, packaging and social posts.

title: Bacàn
creator: Pentagram — Andrea Trabucco-Campos
description: Letterforms expand, collide and overlap like sound waves, expressing the noise of a dinner party. Three weights of a custom geometric typeface create different levels of intensity, while monochrome contrast and overlapping illustrations connect the identity to Italian Futurist and op-art references.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram states that the restaurant reopened in January 2024 with its new identity and environmental graphics.
glyphkiln_test: Control overlap and weight variation while retaining legibility in expressive typographic compositions.

title: The Social Hub
creator: Studio Dumbar/DEPT
description: A flower-like hub symbol joins multiple shapes into one form and takes on illustrated roles, such as a globe or an eye. Bold typography and primary-led colors connect the hotel group’s accommodation, coworking and social spaces across physical and digital applications.
real_world_evidence: Studio Dumbar states that the identity launched with the Madrid hotel and was applied across print, digital, motion and signage.
glyphkiln_test: Transform a single modular brand mark into different illustrations while keeping it recognizable.

title: LenLen
creator: Pentagram — Andrea Trabucco-Campos
description: The restaurant identity combines bubble lettering, street-inspired strokes, informal handwriting and everyday Arial. Loose illustrations of Thai daily life mix with family photographs, while menus, signs and interior murals use deliberate imperfection to evoke the social character of a Thai shophouse.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram credits LenLen’s founders and describes the implemented brand throughout their Manhattan restaurant.
glyphkiln_test: Combine several typographic voices, hand-drawn assets and photo collage without losing hierarchy.

title: Chateau Engalin
creator: Pentagram — Samar Maakaroun
description: Custom letterforms unify a hospitality estate’s varied cultural influences using sauce as the conceptual connection. Pistachio, sumac red, grilled orange and ink-like dark tones draw from the kitchen, supporting an identity intended to move between quiet refinement and exuberant celebrations.
real_world_evidence: Pentagram identifies chef and owner Marwan Badran as client for the redesigned Chateau Engalin identity.
glyphkiln_test: Build a coherent brand across contrasting quiet and celebratory layouts using controlled color and lettering.

title: Nike Run
creator: PORTO ROCHA
description: A RUNSWOOSH lockup, orange and yellow accents, Helvetica Now, and modular layouts join technical running information with emphatic campaign headlines. The system is designed to work across retail, marketing, products, and running events.
real_world_evidence: The studio describes Nike's commission and deployment across global running touchpoints.
glyphkiln_test: Adapt one headline/product system across three aspect ratios without losing technical detail.

title: Nike Be True
creator: PORTO ROCHA
description: The campaign combines documentary and fluid photographic treatments with illustrations by LGBTQIA+ creators. A flexible wordmark and inclusive gradient let different contributors express themselves while the wider campaign stays recognizable.
real_world_evidence: The case study identifies commissioned creators and deployment in billboards, retail takeovers, installations, and film.
glyphkiln_test: Combine multiple image treatments and collaborators' assets under consistent campaign rules.

title: Twitch
creator: PORTO ROCHA
description: The refresh moves between restrained content framing and dense digital expression. Purple, Roobert typography, cutout portraits, dimensional illustrations, sprites, and emotes connect product interfaces with highly expressive communications and TwitchCon installations.
real_world_evidence: The studio reports collaboration with Twitch's creative team and introduction at TwitchCon 2023.
glyphkiln_test: Support both quiet and expressive layout variants in the same brand snapshot.

title: Vevo
creator: PORTO ROCHA
description: Scaling graphic blocks frame artists and content, with secondary colors establishing information hierarchy. Plain typography supports a system that moves between video, static communication, business materials, and data visualization without abandoning its modular structure.
real_world_evidence: The case study names Vevo stakeholders and describes a commissioned identity spanning audiences and channels.
glyphkiln_test: Compose image, text, and statistics in flexible blocks rather than a single repeated layout.

title: Zigzag
creator: PORTO ROCHA
description: A fashion-inspired wordmark and brighter pink palette are paired with Korean and Latin sans serif typography. Editorial images and casual user photography can be cut out and combined with custom 3D stickers for social expression.
real_world_evidence: The studio identifies Zigzag's rebrand, client team, Korean translator, and social sticker applications.
glyphkiln_test: Test Korean/Latin hierarchy, cutout assets, and portrait story compositions.

title: Pollen
creator: PORTO ROCHA
description: A library of pollen-like organic forms can be regrouped around different artists. Flexible color combinations and commissioned portraits express the playlist's human curation, with floral gifts extending the same concept into a launch activation.
real_world_evidence: The studio links to the Spotify playlist and documents commissioned portraits and launch bouquets.
glyphkiln_test: Generate a family of cover variants from seeded shape placement and artist-specific palettes.

title: Melissa Flygrl
creator: PORTO ROCHA
description: Concrete and pastel foam, cursive lettering and condensed display type, and pink and brown create deliberate tension. Campaign photography and set design extend the same contrasts into product and talent imagery across social, commerce, and print.
real_world_evidence: The studio states it was invited to design Melissa's Autumn/Winter 2017 Flygrl identity and campaign.
glyphkiln_test: Pair contrasting type styles and photographic materials while preserving product prominence.

title: Airbnb Tyrus
creator: PORTO ROCHA
description: A strong grid recalls forms, spreadsheets, and calendars while illustrations deliberately break out of that structure. Tiempos and Airbnb Cereal help organize dense guides and templates for illustrators managing clients, time, and budgets.
real_world_evidence: The case study documents a launched Airbnb toolkit and names the commissioned illustrators.
glyphkiln_test: Test dense instructional layouts, mixed illustration styles, and reusable guide components.

title: LinkedIn Year in Review
creator: BUCK
description: Personal statistics drive a modular sequence of animated recap screens. Designed in Rive, the system supports English, Spanish, and Portuguese as well as a broad range of mobile devices, making variable data and localization central production constraints.
real_world_evidence: BUCK describes its collaboration with LinkedIn on the platform's 2025 Year in Review experience.
glyphkiln_test: Stress-test variable names, large numbers, missing statistics, three languages, and reproducible batch generation.

title: WhatsApp Stickers
creator: BUCK
description: Sticker packs use emotional specificity, dimensionality, color, and implied or animated movement. Evergreen characters sit beside culturally specific packs, including a Detty December collaboration with West African artist Yellow Yemisi.
real_world_evidence: BUCK documents WhatsApp's commission, a sticker playbook, and a year of pack development.
glyphkiln_test: Check small-scale readability, transparent assets, character consistency, and localized asset sets.

title: StreetEasy: Let the Journey Begin
creator: BUCK with Mother New York
description: Contemporary New York housing situations are rendered as Renaissance-style paintings, including subway journeys and co-op meetings. Local details reward closer inspection while the same scenes work on station platforms, train takeovers, and a Williamsburg mural.
real_world_evidence: BUCK names StreetEasy and Mother New York and documents subway and mural placements.
source_title: StreetEasy: Let the Journey Begin — BUCK with Mother New York
glyphkiln_test: Preserve detailed commissioned artwork and readable captions across print-like and digital layouts.

title: Spotify Summer Campaign
creator: BUCK
description: Twenty-four varied visuals share a graphic border system. The 2023 campaign extends from social and pasted posters to bus stops, murals, and exceptionally wide digital artworks tailored to specific cities and viewing conditions.
real_world_evidence: BUCK states it worked with Spotify's in-house team and identifies installed placements in several US cities.
glyphkiln_test: Test extreme aspect ratios, shared campaign framing, and variation without duplicate composition.

title: DoorDash App Illustration System
creator: BUCK
description: Nearly 200 illustrations cover food, home, and retail categories. The project prioritizes friendly, recognizable forms that remain clear on small screens, then codifies that visual language in guidelines for internal designers and outside collaborators.
real_world_evidence: BUCK documents DoorDash's product refresh commission and delivery of illustrations and guidelines.
glyphkiln_test: Render a coherent asset library at small sizes and detect loss of distinguishing detail.

title: Square Sydney
creator: BUCK
description: BUCK's Sydney team created a campaign for Square's Australian market across television, social, digital, static advertising, and outdoor placements. The case study contains campaign images and early explorations, offering a production reference for one idea distributed across media.
real_world_evidence: The studio explicitly identifies Square's Australian campaign and credits the client marketing team.
glyphkiln_test: Track approved variants, dimensions, and asset reuse across static and moving deliverables.

title: Facebook Alegria
creator: BUCK
description: A scalable illustration system uses flat geometric shapes, abstract figures, oversized limbs, and nonliteral skin colors. Asset categories extend beyond people to transport, plants, buildings, and hands, supporting consistent scenes across interfaces and print.
real_world_evidence: BUCK says Facebook commissioned the ecosystem redesign in 2017 and describes deployed surfaces.
glyphkiln_test: Compose reusable vector components while preserving a specific illustration grammar.

title: Instagram Motion System
creator: Studio Dumbar/DEPT
description: Motion techniques derive from camera movement, swiping, scrolling, and imperfect human gestures. Shared timing and spatial behavior link expressive marketing with product interactions, backed by templates and guidelines for designers working across the brand.
real_world_evidence: The studio states Instagram invited the collaboration and describes daily use and Penn Plaza campaign deployment.
glyphkiln_test: Define the boundary between static frame generation and repeatable motion templates.

title: NPO Broadcasting Identity
creator: Studio Dumbar/DEPT
description: A diamond symbol, custom typeface, and varied palette unify a family of television, radio, and online channels. The design retains existing recognition while making the parent broadcaster visible across otherwise distinct programming and channel identities.
real_world_evidence: The case study reports implementation across NPO television, radio, and online channels.
glyphkiln_test: Test related sub-brands, logo lockups, and consistent channel-specific colors.

title: Comedy Central Idents
creator: Studio Dumbar/DEPT
description: The wordmark and paired C symbols act as characters, morphing and interacting through comic situations. Timing, physics, and sound create humor across eighteen hero idents and thirteen themed idents rather than relying on a single logo reveal.
real_world_evidence: The case study records a commission from Comedy Central's international creative team.
glyphkiln_test: Identify requirements for shape deformation, timing, and sound beyond static SVG/PNG output.

title: Adidas Futurenatural
creator: Studio Dumbar/DEPT
description: Bespoke lettering and fluid kinetic shapes connect the shoe's technical construction with its anatomical fit. The wordmark is designed for very different production methods, including billboards, embroidery, rubber details, and digital motion.
real_world_evidence: The studio documents intensive collaboration with Adidas's global design team on the footwear identity.
glyphkiln_test: Test a custom mark at tiny product scale and large display scale, with output-method constraints.

title: Music + Talk by Spotify
creator: Studio Dumbar/DEPT
description: Containers around the words stretch and contract with sound-like energy. Their shapes also create cropped and rotated static patterns, allowing a recognizable visual system to work with or without the full wordmark.
real_world_evidence: The studio says it was selected for the identity and delivered accessible brand assets and guidelines.
source_title: Music + Talk by Spotify — Studio Dumbar/DEPT
glyphkiln_test: Turn one core shape language into deterministic patterns and distinct communication variants.

title: MTV VMAs 2022
creator: Studio Dumbar/DEPT
description: Artist footage sits inside room-like VMA letterforms that tilt and rotate. Chunky Signs typography and vivid color support a campaign spanning nominees, categories, television, social, and large outdoor screens, with static and animated needs considered together.
real_world_evidence: MTV commissioned the campaign identity; the studio documents delivered assets and a Penn Plaza placement.
glyphkiln_test: Test image masks inside lettering, variable artist content, and static/motion consistency.

title: Uber: Your Nearest Driver Is Minutes Away
creator: Mother
description: Regional place names and short arrival-time messages sit over cinematic street photographs of nights out and bad weather. Small route-like symbols frame the copy while a clear Uber wordmark anchors the corner, keeping locally specific scenes within one consistent outdoor system.
real_world_evidence: Mother identifies the regional awareness campaign and includes five outdoor advertising applications.
source_title: Uber: Your Nearest Uber Driver is Minutes Away — Mother
glyphkiln_test: Adapt regional copy across a series while maintaining clear service and brand hierarchy.

title: IKEA: Hidden Prices
creator: Mother
description: Photographed products obscure their prices, making the visual idea about quality before cost. Strong colored backdrops and a tightly controlled product focus allow one concept to extend across different home-furnishing items.
real_world_evidence: Mother identifies the OOH campaign and photographer Marloes Haarmans.
glyphkiln_test: Support intentional text/image occlusion while distinguishing it from accidental unreadability.

title: McDonald's: Follow the Arches
creator: Cossette
description: Cropped fragments of the golden arches become directional signals with very little text. The campaign uses familiar brand geometry as both the identifying mark and the message, adapting to different routes toward nearby restaurants.
real_world_evidence: Cossette documents four deployed Toronto-area boards, three static and one digital, with McDonald's Canada credited.
glyphkiln_test: Test intentional logo cropping, direction-specific variants, and instant-distance readability.

title: Nike Women Korea VaporMax
creator: Wieden+Kennedy Tokyo; graphic design by Dasol Jung
description: Female Korean athletes appear in reimagined Seoul settings with Korean typography and campaign lockups. Athlete-specific posters and looping visuals combine local context with a shared launch system suited to social and a very long subway display.
real_world_evidence: The participating designer names Nike and W+K Tokyo and describes social rollout and a 100-meter Seoul digital board.
source_title: Nike Women Korea VaporMax — Wieden+Kennedy Tokyo; graphic design by Dasol Jung
glyphkiln_test: Test Hangul/Latin typography and coherent image sequences across extreme display dimensions.

title: WSJ: Missing Articles
creator: Mother
description: Blank newspaper areas represent reporting that detained journalist Evan Gershkovich could not produce. The concept turns editorial absence into the campaign's central graphic device, making empty space carry meaning inside a familiar publication format.
real_world_evidence: Mother identifies the newspaper intervention marking one year of Gershkovich's detention on March 29, 2024.
glyphkiln_test: Preserve intentional empty space within a dense editorial grid instead of auto-filling it.

title: Uber Reserve: Origami
creator: Mother
description: Event tickets fold into small car forms against black fields. The paper object connects the occasion with the reserved journey, leaving a simple focal point and turning a service proposition into a tangible photographic metaphor.
real_world_evidence: Mother identifies the work as an OOH campaign for Uber Reserve.
glyphkiln_test: Combine detailed cutout objects, dark backgrounds, and concise service copy without crushing texture.

title: Uber Eats: Iftar Incoming
creator: Mother
description: One campaign execution produces hundreds of localized variants. Poster content changes each day to show the local sunset time during Ramadan, demonstrating how a simple communication system can carry accurate date- and place-specific information.
real_world_evidence: Mother states that posters were customized by location and updated daily throughout the month.
glyphkiln_test: Batch render validated date, time, and location data with provenance and overflow checks.

title: KFC: Vertically Gifted
creator: Mother
description: An oversized Tower Burger is rotated to dominate a wide billboard, with condensed white lettering running along red side strips. The subject's height drives the composition and turns a format constraint into the campaign's visual joke.
real_world_evidence: Mother presents the work as a KFC Tower Burger campaign with installed outdoor examples.
glyphkiln_test: Allow intentional rotation and extreme crops while keeping the product and essential copy recognizable.

title: IKEA: One Bag to Rule Them All
creator: Mother
description: IKEA blue bags filled with varied shopping and home objects anchor the Oxford Street launch. Close product views become posters, while repeated full-length shoppers create an expansive station takeover, linking a small retail object to much larger public surfaces.
real_world_evidence: Mother explicitly connects the campaign to the opening at 214 Oxford Street.
source_title: IKEA: One Bag to Rule Them All — Mother
glyphkiln_test: Build a retail-launch family around a recognizable product asset and location/date hierarchy.
